answer: Time-locked staking binds capital to identity and kills the forger's turnover rate. An identity locks 150 units for 20 epochs, 5% freed per honest epoch, and the stake stays illiquid, so 150,000 units behind 1,000 fakes cannot be recycled. Cheating slashes 60% and resets the timer, adding 10 epochs of illiquidity per offence. Honest agents recover gradually and face only opportunity cost; a forger caught at 30% loses 27,000 units. The karst-hard logic: the zephyr of cheap forgery meets a gale of frozen capital, and each offence lengthens the freeze.
